# LegatorOCR v0.2.0-pre.51 (pre-release)

Written and tried by the author's assistant on one Linux machine; the automated tests pass on CI runners. **Nothing was tried by hand on Windows, macOS or arm64.**

**Fingers on photographed pages (from the tester's book photos)**
- A hand holding the book is now wiped whole: the other fingers, which a crease or a shadow keeps from touching the border, go with the one that does; a skin blob within ~1.5 mm of the border counts as touching it; the dark warm creases between fingers no longer count as print (that made the program leave the finger alone), and the shadowed rim is painted over (grown by 1 mm). Tried on one photo (IMG_20261112_191951, thumb and two fingers): the hand is gone except for a few thin slivers in the creases. Not tried on other photos; the effect on pages without a hand is covered by the existing tests only.
- Two new tests (a hand of three fingers, and the quality-report note).

**Adversarial audit (hostile files and extreme options)**
Tried with the release build, with a 10 GB memory cap and a 90 s limit per run: ~60 hostile files (empty, truncated, random bytes, 1x1 / 100000x1 / 60000x60000 pictures, PDFs with cyclic page trees, form cycles, a flate bomb, a claimed 100000x100000 image, a /Count of a billion, a zip and a tar.gz bomb, a zip with `../` members, a TIFF with an IFD loop, file names with spaces, a newline and a leading dash), 54 extreme option values (dpi, skew, page size, erase and work areas, cut angle, keystone, thresholds, output dpi, margins, colours), 150 random mutations of a project file, and 24 odd search queries. Found and fixed:
- A picture header claiming 60000 x 60000 pixels (10.8 GB) aborted the program on the allocation; it is now refused with a message (also in the WebAssembly build).
- A PDF or TIFF claiming a billion pages aborted the program (24 GB); the count is now limited by what the file's size allows (at most 200 000) and a warning is printed.
- Folders of extracted archives left by a run that was killed stayed in the temp folder for ever; the next run now removes those of dead processes (Linux) and any older than a week, only folders of its own name and owner.
- `--article-query ""` was accepted and did nothing; it is now an error. Article pictures of two files with the same name no longer overwrite each other.
Nothing else broke: no panic, hang or runaway memory in the other cases. A 468-byte PDF that claims a huge image takes 23 s because the external renderer (pdftoppm) is slow on it; not changed.
**What this is not**: not a full audit of 80 000 lines. The graphical window, signing, encryption, the e-invoice, BagIt and EPUB checks, Windows/macOS and arm64 were not fuzzed here. "All problems fixed" cannot be claimed.

**Tinted paper**: `--quality-report` now says when the paper of the photos is cream or yellow, and that `--remove-background` (GUI: remove background) makes it white. Colour output still keeps the paper's own tone by default.

**Known and not done**: a PDF made from large colour pages can stay far over the target size, because the target only lowers the JPEG quality (floor 30); lowering the resolution is not done. Right-hand text cut at the gutter of curved photographed pages is not fixed.

**Not verified**: Windows, macOS, arm64. On the macOS Intel runner (experimental) two PKCS#12 tests fail because of its OpenSSL, unrelated.
